searchText: From my understanding the peer scoring is mostly up to implementation. If a client is too restrictive then it would likely struggle finding and maintaining a pool of peers so this is kind of self-regulating. Not well aware of the Prysm implementation in particular, but the logic could be to downscore offline nodes to reduce the number of further reconnect attempts. If it prevents inbound connections from this node, then it's likely a bug. when was EIP-8080 discussed and approved? can someone point me to the thread or channel? AFAIK 8080 was separated from 8061 specifically cause the latter was much simpler to implement. Are you certain that 8080 is scheduled to be included? my memory is not the best, but I recall differently https://forkcast.org/eips/8080 https://forkcast.org/calls/acdc/179?search=8080&timestamp=01:08:06&type=agenda&text=EIP-8080%20(exits%20use%20consolidation%20queue)%3A%20intent%20to%20DFI%3B%20decision%20deferred%20two%20weeks per what <@755590043632140352> notes, it looks like it's closer to DFI than anything else > Parithosh Jayanthi:Okay, maybe to be fair to client teams, we shouldn't make the decision here right now to DFI [EIP-8080], but at least give intent that we plan on DFI. DFI means decide for inclusion? it does not mean that, no DFI is a rejection https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7723#declined-for-inclusion thank you https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7773 ok so nothing to fix the loophole in consolidations is going into glamsterdam? given EIP-8071 has already been rejected? well, that's one way of framing it a bit of a leading question. I'll just say that, EIP-8061 is part of Glamsterdam, EIP-8071 not, and looks like EIP-8080 also not. Obviously the relative priority or recognition or agreement different people might have of whether there's a "loophole in consolidations" to "fix" is subjective and individual I get what you mean. I tried to get involved in the discussion here: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8080-let-exits-use-the-consolidation-queue/26552 but honestly just tumbleweed frustrating to find out what is happening, so I really appreciate your reply here 🙂 In general these are discussed in biweekly ACDC calls, but to be fair, while those are public, they tend to be core dev-oriented

excerpts.author: nashatyrev
excerpts.content:
From my understanding the peer scoring is mostly up to implementation. If a client is too restrictive then it would likely struggle finding and maintaining a pool of peers so this is kind of self-regulating. 
Not well aware of the Prysm implementation in particular, but the logic could be to downscore  offline nodes to reduce the number of further reconnect attempts. If it prevents inbound connections from this node, then it's likely a bug.
